title: Legislation Amendment (Sunsetting Review and Other Measures) Bill 2018
short_title: Legislation Amendment (Sunsetting Review and Other Measures) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would revise the framework for automatically repealing older legislative instruments and make technical changes to federal legislation and statutory interpretation rules.
It would widen the Attorney-General's powers to defer expiry dates or align them for related instruments, while adding parliamentary scrutiny of those decisions.
The bill would also clarify retrospective commencement, incorporation of earlier documents and correction of errors on the Federal Register of Legislation, subject to safeguards.
changes: Federal court rules would be exempt from automatic expiry while retaining registration, publication and parliamentary disallowance requirements.
Parliament's power to extend an instrument's expiry date would no longer be subject to the existing time restriction.
A sitting day would mean a day a parliamentary House actually sat, with rules for sittings continuing across calendar days.
Corrected versions of previously tabled, disallowable instruments would generally require fresh tabling and a new disallowance period.
summary.affected: The Attorney-General, federal courts, Parliament, Commonwealth rule-makers and the First Parliamentary Counsel would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Christian Porter
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the Legislation Amendment (Sunsetting Review and Other Measures) Bill 2018 to implement recommendations from a review of sunsetting provisions, including broadening the Attorney-General’s power to defer sunsetting, removing time restrictions on parliamentary rollovers, exempting federal court rules from sunsetting, and clarifying definitions and protections around retrospective commencement and error correction.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: The Legislation Amendment (Sunsetting Review and Other Measures) Bill 2018 makes technical amendments to harmonise sunsetting provisions, implementing 45 recommendations from a 2017 review by Anderson, Quiggin and Larkins. Labor supports the bill, noting the sunsetting framework has removed or replaced 60% of 2,024 listed legislative instruments since 2003.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The Legislation Amendment (Sunsetting Review and Other Measures) Bill 2018 was commended to the House as improving Commonwealth legislative frameworks and supporting regulatory reform. It implements recommendations requiring legislative action from the report on sunsetting provisions in the Legislation Act 2003 and makes minor technical amendments to that Act and the Acts Interpretation Act.
